# CLI reference

Every command of `agent-resend`, generated from the CLI itself.

The CLI needs no MCP server and no agent. Install `@agentcomms/resend` and run it.

```bash
npx -y @agentcomms/resend <command>          # without installing
npm i -g @agentcomms/resend && agent-resend   # or on the PATH
```

`<angle brackets>` are required, `[square brackets]` optional, `<name...>` repeats. Every command takes
`--json` for a machine-readable envelope, and `--no-color` to drop ANSI codes.

## Exit codes

Scripts should read these rather than parse output.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | unexpected failure |
| `10` | a send or a change was refused or needs approval |
| `11` | a newer release is out: update first (`agentcomms update`), or put it off until tomorrow (`agentcomms update --later`) |
| `64` | the command was used wrongly |
| `65` | the data given was not usable |
| `66` | what was asked for does not exist |
| `69` | Resend or the secret store is unavailable |
| `75` | temporary; retrying later is reasonable |
| `77` | sign-in or a permission is needed |
| `78` | a configuration problem, including `doctor` finding something broken |

## Commands

| Command | What it is for |
|---|---|
| [`account`](#agent-resend-account) | connect, inspect, re-police and remove Resend accounts |
| [`doctor`](#agent-resend-doctor) | check what has to work, and say who enforces what — read-only is this package’s promise, not the key’s |
| [`domains`](#agent-resend-domains) | the team’s domains and their status; with --domain, the DNS records one needs |
| [`emails`](#agent-resend-emails) | sent emails: what went, and what happened to it |
| [`received`](#agent-resend-received) | received emails — untrusted content, shown with Resend’s SPF, DKIM and DMARC results |
| [`metrics`](#agent-resend-metrics) | delivery, bounce and complaint counts; the last 7 days unless --start and --end say otherwise |
| [`suppressions`](#agent-resend-suppressions) | addresses Resend will not send to, and why |
| [`send`](#agent-resend-send) | prepare an email, and send it once a person has approved it |
| [`scheduled`](#agent-resend-scheduled) | emails waiting to be sent at a later time |
| [`approve`](#agent-resend-approve) | approve a send or a change at this terminal: read it, then type the code back |
| [`mcp`](#agent-resend-mcp) | run the MCP server on stdio, for a coding agent to connect to |

### `agent-resend account`

connect, inspect, re-police and remove Resend accounts

```
agent-resend account [options] [command]
```

### `agent-resend account add`

connect a Resend API key, typed by a person at this terminal (or RESEND_API_KEY); never from a chat

```
agent-resend account add [options] <name>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode <mode>` | read (the default for a full-access key) or send (choices: "read", "send") | — |
| `--send <policy>` | how its sends are approved; the machine default if left out (choices: "chat", "confirm", "never") | — |
| `--domain <domain>` | for a sending-only key restricted to one domain: that domain | — |
| `--approval <approvalId>` | apply a change a person approved: said yes to in chat, or approved with the approve command it gave | — |

### `agent-resend account list`

the Resend accounts this machine can use, and what each may do

```
agent-resend account list [options]
```

### `agent-resend account show`

one account: its key’s permission, its mode, its send policy, and who enforces what

```
agent-resend account show [options] <name>
```

### `agent-resend account remove`

forget an account and delete its key, once a person approves it

```
agent-resend account remove [options] <name>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--approval <approvalId>` | apply a change a person approved: said yes to in chat, or approved with the approve command it gave | — |

### `agent-resend account policy`

report how its sends and changes are approved, or set --send, --mode and --change; loosening is approved by a person

```
agent-resend account policy [options] <name>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--send <policy>` | chat, confirm or never | — |
| `--mode <mode>` | read or send | — |
| `--change <policy>` | how a loosening of this account is approved: chat or confirm | — |
| `--approval <approvalId>` | apply a change a person approved: said yes to in chat, or approved with the approve command it gave | — |

### `agent-resend doctor`

check what has to work, and say who enforces what — read-only is this package’s promise, not the key’s

```
agent-resend doctor [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | check only this account | — |
| `--offline` | do not ask Resend anything | `false` |

|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which account, as `organisation/resend` | — |

### `agent-resend send`

prepare an email, and send it once a person has approved it

```
agent-resend send [options] [command]
```

### `agent-resend send prepare`

build an email and show exactly what would go, to whom. Sends nothing

```
agent-resend send prepare [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which account, as `organisation/resend` | — |
| `--from <address>` | the sender, at a verified domain: `Name <you@example.com>` or a bare address | — |
| `--to <address>` | a recipient; repeat for more | `[]` |
| `--cc <address>` | a copy recipient; repeat for more | `[]` |
| `--bcc <address>` | a blind recipient; repeat for more — the preview lists every one | `[]` |
| `--subject <subject>` | the subject | — |
| `--text <text>` | the plain-text body | — |
| `--html <html>` | an HTML body whose visible text is the text body; no images, forms or hidden parts | — |
| `--attach <path>` | a file to attach, from an allowed folder; repeat for more | `[]` |
| `--reply-to <address>` | where replies go; repeat for more | `[]` |
| `--in-reply-to <messageId>` | the Message-ID this replies to, to keep the thread | — |
| `--references <messageId>` | an earlier Message-ID in the thread; repeat for more | `[]` |
| `--scheduled-at <time>` | send later: an ISO 8601 time with a zone, at most 30 days ahead | — |

### `agent-resend send execute`

send a prepared email by approval id; optional legacy expectations are checked exactly

```
agent-resend send execute [options] <approvalId>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which account, as `organisation/resend` | — |
| `--expect-to <addresses>` | legacy exact check: To list, comma-separated, or none | — |
| `--expect-cc <addresses>` | legacy exact check: Cc list, or none | — |
| `--expect-bcc <addresses>` | legacy exact check: Bcc list, or none | — |
| `--expect-subject <subject>` | legacy exact check: subject | — |

### `agent-resend send status`

what happened to a send — the local record, and Resend’s last event. Never sends again

```
agent-resend send status [options] <approvalId>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | which account, as `organisation/resend` | — |

### `agent-resend send wait`

wait for an approval to be usable or finished, and say where it stands — it only looks, and never sends

```
agent-resend send wait [options] <approvalId>
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--wait-seconds <n>` | how long to wait: 30 when left out, 300 at most, 0 for the status now | — |

|---|---|---|

approve a send or a change at this terminal: read it, then type the code back


### `agent-resend mcp`

run the MCP server on stdio, for a coding agent to connect to

```
agent-resend mcp [options] [command]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--account <name>` | pin the server to one account; every tool then acts on it and no other | — |

### `agent-resend mcp install`

register this server with an MCP client, and prove it starts

```
agent-resend mcp install [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--client <client>` | which client to register with (choices: "claude-code", "claude-desktop", "codex", "cursor", "gemini", "vscode", "json") | — |
| `--name <name>` | the name the client will show: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens | `"resend"` |
| `--account <name>` | pin the server to one account | — |
| `--launcher <launcher>` | how the server is started (choices: "managed", "npx", "local") | — |
| `--no-verify` | do not start the server to check the entry works | — |
| `--force` | replace this server's own earlier entry — this is how you upgrade | `false` |
| `--print` | only print what would be written | `false` |
| `--approval <approvalId>` | register the server this approval was given for | — |

### `agent-resend mcp prune`

remove managed runtimes that no client config it can read names, no printed entry names, and no process runs

```
agent-resend mcp prune [options]
```

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | only say what would be removed | `false` |
| `--include-printed` | also remove runtimes kept only because an entry for them was printed (--client json, --print), once those entries are gone | `false` |
| `--approval <approvalId>` | remove the runtimes this approval was given for | — |
